description: Baseline: frozen regex corpus on unmodified release interpreter (sum of 8 case totals).

asi.corpus: scripts/regex-bench.josh frozen; release binary; single run
asi.hypotheses: see autoresearch.ideas.md; heaviest cases astral-group(356) + literal-long(~375 est) then date-extract(205)
asi.note: single-run bench; per-case totals printed as diagnostics; hits checksum 315 stable

description: COW frames: caller-frame Arc<Frame> sharing in call_function (no per-call BTreeMap clone); two-frame push keeps params separate; assign is copy-on-write via Arc::make_mut; snapshot semantics preserved. Matches profile: clone_subtree + BTreeMap insert/drop + String clone ≈12% of samples.

asi.hypothesis: per-user-function-call full clone of captured BTreeMap frame (engine.rs call_function)
asi.evidence: sample profile clone_subtree 4.3%, BTreeMap insert 2.8%, IntoIter drop 3.0%, String::clone 4.0%
asi.delta: -12.5% vs baseline; groups-anchored -30%, nfa-stress -18%; literals modest
asi.next: snapshot() flatten O(n) per closure creation; Value clone/Arc churn inside re_add_thread; eval_program 7.3%

description: Frame BTreeMap to HashMap: no gain (1555 vs kept 1539). SipHash on short String keys loses to BTreeMap comparisons at these frame sizes; completion ordering then needed sorted anyway.

asi.hypothesis: BTreeMap memcmp/traversal hot; HashMap O(1) wins
asi.learning: frame maps are small (5-60 keys); BTreeMap fine; seek alloc reductions instead

description: Fast-path BindingPattern::Name in bind_pattern: direct frame insert, skip reject_reserved_pattern recursion, Vec alloc, and collect_bindings walk. Hit once per function argument per call.

asi.hypothesis: bind_pattern+collect_bindings ~5.6% of samples; simple ident params dominate call overhead
asi.next: eval_block frame per if/while body; eval_call_args Vec; chars.get index path; ArrayValue::snapshot per slice

description: index_value array fast path: get_indexed under a single RwLock read (negative-index resolution inline) instead of snapshot()-cloning the whole Vec per access. Was the benchmark's dominant cost.

asi.hypothesis: index_value (Array, Int) cloned entire Vec via snapshot() per element access; chars[sp] with len 1506 per VM char-step
asi.verified: hits_total 315 stable across all iterations; lengths identical
asi.next: astral-group now dominates (238ms): suspect per-piece closure allocs in units-map build (chars[i].length) and SAVE-heavy thread churn

description: Frame becomes a small-enum: Vec<(String, Value)> linear scan up to 8 entries, spilling to BTreeMap. Kills per-call BTreeMap insert/rebalance/IntoIter-drop for the params frame.

asi.hypothesis: per-call params-frame BTreeMap insert + node-walk drop ≈7.5% of samples
asi.next: astral-group 225ms still dominant — next investigate per-sp re_fresh_caps (2-slot arrays × allocation chains) and String pc-key formatting in added_cur

description: Skip the per-call self-name String alloc + frame insert for named functions already pointer-identically visible in scope. Recursion unchanged; param shadowing order preserved.

asi.note: top-level regex fns resolve via root frame, saving alloc+insert per call of named fns
asi.next: flattening; remaining costs are per-op Value churn inherent to immutable array/object value semantics

description: Pre-size experiment: Vec::with_capacity(4) for Frame::Small + with_capacity for call args. Consistent +1.4% regression (592-593 vs 584 across two runs): empty block frames eagerly allocate 96B and small/empty calls over-allocate.

asi.learning: lazy 0-cap Vec is optimal here because many frames stay empty (if/while blocks) and most calls have few args

description: Capture-cache: RefCell<HashMap<Arc-ptr, per-frame name map>> for captured-frame variable resolution. Regressed (638 vs 584): RefCell borrows + double hash probing + strong_count atomics cost more than the BTreeMap walk saved. Dead-code clippy warning (keeper field never read) also tripped checks.

asi.learning: hashmap-of-hashmaps caching loses to direct small-map scan; variable resolution needs fewer LOOKUPS, not a memo
asi.next_action_hint: attack lookup COUNT: closure-heavy call edges and eval_expr dispatch, or string comparisons in Small get via len+first-byte prefilter

description: Frame as single sorted Vec with binary search (replacing Small/BTree hybrid). +4% regression (607 vs 584): per-call param inserts gained binary-search+memmove costs while big-frame lookup locality gains were smaller.

asi.learning: Small(BTreeMap hybrid) beats uniform sorted-vec: O(1)-append param insertion dominates over lookup locality

description: Array slice single-copy: ArrayValue::slice_range clones only [lo..hi] under one read lock; used by eval_slice (a[lo..hi]) and Array.prototype.slice (replacing snapshot() full-Vec clone + second range clone). Verification run 2: 570 total, astral-group 210.

asi.delta_vs_prev_best: 585 vs 584 within noise run1; run2 570 confirms ~-2%
asi.astral_group: slice-heavy case 219 to 212/210 across runs as predicted

description: Exact-size hot allocations: params frame Vec::with_capacity(params.len()) in call_function, args Vec with_capacity(args.len()) in eval_call_args. Kills 1-2 realloc steps per call; empty block frames stay lazy.

asi.learning: isolating capacity ALL-defined call paths works; blanket pre-sizing regressed

description: resolve_prototype_member: fixed 16-entry visited window instead of per-call Vec alloc; chains are tiny. Samples 584/544/576/558 (median ~567) vs prior best 568: statistically neutral; kept as strictly-fewer-allocations simplification.

asi.noise_note: per-case values roaming ±10% run to run (thermal); four samples taken
asi.verdict: neutral metric, kept for less mechanical work per method lookup

description: Global allocator swap to mimalloc (josh-cli). Alloc-heavy interpreter: every case dropped 25-30% uniformly.

asi.learning: system allocator (macOS) was ~27% of runtime; uniform per-case improvement 25-30% confirms allocator-bound hypothesis
asi.next: re-profile under mimalloc: Arc refcounters and Value drop traffic may now dominate

description: call_function consumes args via into_iter() instead of args.get(i).cloned() per param — removes one Arc clone/drop pair per argument per call. Metric-neutral (413 = best) but strictly less work and simpler.

Small-string optimization: Value::String payload Arc<str> -> compact_str::CompactString (inline <=24B). Removes per-char-string allocations (regex chars arrays), refcount traffic on clones. Neutral under mimalloc (413/412) - kept as premise for the mimalloc-ablation experiment.

asi.verdict: neutral under mimalloc; kept for ablation premise
asi.learning: allocation-count reductions are invisible once mimalloc is in - mimalloc made per-alloc ~free
asi.next: ablate mimalloc: if system+SSO tie mimalloc, allocator dependency can be dropped

description: MIMALLOC ABLATION: system allocator + SSO = 549ms vs mimalloc+SSO = 413ms. mimalloc still worth -25%; restored. Bonus: SSO itself = -3.3% under system alloc (549 vs 568 pre-mimalloc best), previously masked.

Frame free-list pool (LIFO reuse of params/block frames). +7% regression (443/446 vs 413): mimalloc already makes Arc alloc/free ~free, so pooling adds bookkeeping (try_unwrap, pool ops, reserve checks) without removing real work.

asi.learning: under mimalloc, allocation ELIMINATION is worthless; only removing actual WORK wins
asi.next_action_hint: stop pathway near: remaining profile is dispatch + frame-get; next big swing would be compile-time (AST arena flattening or interned variable slots)

description: String concat: replace format!('{left}{right}') with in-place push_str on moved left operand, then wrap. Removes format machinery + double allocation per concat (hot: per-NFA-thread marker keys). 408/408 consistent vs 413.

asi.note: bounded-mechanism keep; remaining structural swings (interning, AST arena) documented as out-of-loop-scope in ideas file

description: ObjectValue lazy side-index (HashMap) for >16-entry objects; prototypes are 33 entries so index built. 411 vs 408 = neutral: object key scans were never hot enough to matter; added machinery not justified.

asi.learning: ObjectValue::get profile attribution (~1.5%) was misleading - once mimalloc + SSO in, remaining named hotspots under-evaluate

description: Release profile: lto=fat + codegen-units=1. Three samples {429 (post-build thermal), 398, 400} -> median ~399 vs prior 408 = -2% real. Cross-crate inlining of hot engine/value/natives paths.

asi.note: first sample polluted by post-LTO-build thermal

description: target-cpu=native via .cargo/config.toml: samples {437, 413, 413} median 413 vs LTO-only 399 = +3.5% regression (code-layout luck against us); also machine-specific binaries would hurt distribution.

asi.learning: generic target-cpu layout is luck-neutral-positive; native specialization not free
